description: Prompts a product engineer would plausibly write, each targeting a rule the skill is supposed to enforce. An answer that violates an expectation means the rule is not landing — fix the rule's wording before adding more rules.

evals.prompt: In our Vue 3 app using @youcan/celeste, build a settings card with a title, some muted description text, and a Save button. Give it a white background, 16px padding and rounded corners.
evals.expected_output: A component whose styles are entirely token references, using Button from the library.
expectations: Uses `var(--spacing-16)` rather than a literal 16px
Uses `var(--radius-*)` rather than a literal border-radius
Uses `var(--color-bg-white-0)` rather than #fff or white
Uses `var(--color-text-sub-600)` for the muted text, not a neutral primitive or a hex value
Uses `font: var(--label-*)` or another typography shorthand rather than font-size
Imports Button from @youcan/celeste rather than styling a raw <button>

evals.prompt: Our Celeste app needs to support dark mode on this panel component. Make sure it looks right in dark.
evals.expected_output: No new dark-mode CSS; semantic tokens used throughout, with an explanation that theming is automatic.
expectations: Does NOT add a [data-theme='dark'] block or a prefers-color-scheme media query
Does NOT add dark-specific colour values
Replaces any hard-coded or primitive colours with semantic tokens
Explains that semantic tokens re-theme automatically and that data-theme is set on an ancestor

evals.prompt: Add a status indicator to this row using @youcan/celeste. It shows success, warning, or error, each with its own icon.
evals.expected_output: StatusBadge, or a lookup map of complete icon class strings — never an interpolated icon name.
expectations: Does NOT build the icon class by interpolation, e.g. `i-celeste-${status}-fill`
Either uses StatusBadge, or maps each state to a complete literal class string
If StatusBadge is used, does not also pass an icon — it derives one from `state`
Renders icons as a class on an element, not as an imported icon component

evals.prompt: I need a primary call-to-action button at the bottom of this onboarding page, plus a cancel option next to it.
evals.expected_output: One FancyButton for the CTA and a lower-emphasis Button or LinkButton for cancel.
expectations: Uses FancyButton for the single primary call to action
Does NOT use FancyButton for both buttons
Uses Button (e.g. neutral or ghost variant) or LinkButton for cancel
Sets emphasis through variant/intent props rather than custom CSS

evals.prompt: Set up @youcan/celeste in a fresh Vue 3 + Vite app.
evals.expected_output: Both CSS imports in the right order, plugin or named-import registration.
expectations: Imports @youcan/celeste-tokens/tokens.css as well as @youcan/celeste/assets/celeste.css
Imports the token CSS before the component CSS
Explains that celeste.css does not define the tokens it uses
Registers components via the Celeste plugin or by importing them directly

evals.prompt: Make this Celeste Button wider and give it our brand purple background.
evals.expected_output: Layout via class, a pushback on the colour override, or a token-based approach.
expectations: Uses the `class` prop for width/layout only
Does NOT override the button's background with a raw colour value
Points to the existing intent/variant props, or flags that a new brand colour belongs in the tokens package
Does not restyle the component's typography through class

evals.prompt: Build a data table with sortable columns, pagination, and an empty state, using our design system.
evals.expected_output: Composed from the library's Table parts, Pagination, and TableEmpty.
expectations: Looks up the component registry rather than assuming prop names
Composes Table sub-components (TableHeader, TableRow, TableCell, …) rather than raw <table> markup
Uses the library's Pagination component rather than hand-rolled page controls
Uses TableEmpty rather than a custom empty-state div

evals.prompt: What props does Celeste's Combobox take?
evals.expected_output: An answer read out of the shipped registry, not recalled.
expectations: Reads node_modules/@youcan/celeste/ai/component-registry.md rather than answering from memory
Greps for the specific component rather than reading the whole file
Reports props with their actual union values and defaults
Does not invent props from another design system's Combobox

evals.prompt: Add a GitHub sign-in button to the login form.
evals.expected_output: SocialButton with brand="github" and no icon passed.
expectations: Uses SocialButton rather than composing Button with a GitHub icon
Passes brand="github"
Does NOT pass an icon — the provider mark is automatic

evals.prompt: Our sidebar needs a divider between sections and a small icon-only button to collapse it.
evals.expected_output: Existing library components rather than styled divs.
expectations: Uses ContentDivider or the sidebar's own separator rather than a styled div or <hr>
Uses CompactButton for the icon-only control rather than Button with custom sizing
Passes the icon to CompactButton via its required `icon` prop, not as a child
